findings.claim: New in 32213899, against Firstmate decision react-forms-w1-message. The decision's rationale says load failures 'are unreadable forms and must receive the general safe unreadable message', but its operative instruction says to change verify-learner-test.mjs only so that the no-runnable branch is taken only when no test file in the control report failed. 32213899 implements the operative instruction exactly. A control run whose learner test file fails to load therefore skips the no-runnable branch (line 71) and falls to the existing not-clean branch, which prints the unchanged-copy message (lines 76-77: 'your test fails against an unchanged copy of your finished form, so it depends on something other than the form's behaviour.'). It never reaches the general unreadable-form message (line 96), which is printed only when a variant run reports an unreadable form. Observed on macOS (darwin), Node 24.2.0 and npm 11.3.0, in a 0700 scratch copy made with git archive of 32213899 (3221389971fd9a1610de7b60b96b85fcc2daf00d), with the private overlay copied over the starter, npm ci in tests/ and TMPDIR pointed at a private scratch directory. Learner tests were the overlay's reference test and probes I derived from it in scratch, not independently written tests. Learner-side load failure: I added to the reference test a module-level guard that throws only when the imported default export is not the learner's own component, so the file loads in the normal run and fails to load under the mutation config. Harness-side load failure: I appended a module-level throw to a scratch copy of tests/task8-variant.jsx and ran the reference test (restored afterwards; sha256 d85eae98... rechecked). Both throws carried a distinctive marker string. Both got the unchanged-copy message and exit 1. Learner-safe: the verdict is exit 1, no weak test can be accepted this way, the suite error is not printed (the marker string appeared in no output) and no solution code is revealed. Accuracy is mixed. For the learner-side probe the message fits, because that test really does depend on something other than the form's behaviour (it inspects what it imported). For the harness-side case it is not accurate: a correct test that has just passed the normal run is told it depends on something other than the form, with no hint that the check itself could not load. This is the same message c68e4995 gave for this case, and the loop-6 reconciliation recorded it as a residual. So the result falls short of the decision's rationale sentence read literally, while it matches the operative instruction and the loop-6 reconciler's fix direction. It is not an author error. The unreadable-form message the rationale names would not be accurate either: it tells the learner to keep each field's label text inside the <form> element, which has nothing to do with a load failure and would send them to change correct markup.
findings.recommendation: Firstmate to confirm which reading of react-forms-w1-message governs. Recommended for v1: accept the implemented behaviour as matching the operative instruction, and record that the rationale sentence is superseded on this point. Do not route load failures to the label message, because its advice would misdirect. If an accurate message is wanted later, the smallest change is one fixed, learner-safe message for a control run with a failed test file and no assertion results. It could say that the check could not load the test file under the check even though it ran in the normal suite, and tell the learner to run npm test again and report it if it persists, without printing the suite error. That is a new message, so it needs a new decision. Low; it does not justify a further correction loop. Consolidate with sme-fcc-x1.
